experiment_plans.feasibility_notes: The hypothesis is feasible given the available data and compute resources. The UCI Adult Census Income dataset (uci_adult_census_income.csv) contains rich socioeconomic indicators suitable for clustering, including age, education, marital status, occupation, and income. This dataset allows for the implementation of K-means with PCA, hierarchical clustering, and fuzzy c-means methods without requiring additional data downloads. The experiment can be conducted within typical SLURM GPU node time limits (hours to days) using standard Python libraries like scikit-learn and pandas.
experiment_plans.objective: To determine whether K-means clustering with PCA dimensionality reduction recovers income strata more consistently with predefined income thresholds than hierarchical clustering or fuzzy c-means methods.

independent: survey indicators related to income and socioeconomic status (age, education, marital status, occupation, capital gain, capital loss, hours per week)
dependent: cluster assignments from different clustering methods (K-means with PCA, hierarchical clustering, fuzzy c-means)

experiment_plans.design: Comparative benchmark experiment using three clustering methods (K-means with PCA, hierarchical clustering, fuzzy c-means) on the same preprocessed socioeconomic dataset. Each method is applied to the same feature set, and the resulting clusters are evaluated against predefined income thresholds using consistency metrics.

data_requirements.description: The UCI Adult Census Income dataset contains demographic and economic features of individuals including age, education, marital status, occupation, capital gains/losses, and hours worked per week, along with income level ('>50K' or '<=50K'). This dataset provides the necessary socioeconomic indicators for clustering and allows for comparison with predefined income thresholds.
preprocessing_steps: Remove the 'fnlwgt' column (sampling weight) as it's not a feature
Encode categorical variables (workclass, education, marital_status, occupation, relationship, race, sex, native_country) using one-hot encoding
Normalize numerical features (age, capital_gain, capital_loss, hours_per_week) using StandardScaler
Create binary target variable from 'income' column ('>50K' = 1, '<=50K' = 0) for threshold comparison
Select features that represent income and socioeconomic status indicators

methods.name: K-means clustering
methods.description: Applies K-means algorithm to group individuals into clusters based on socioeconomic features. Uses elbow method to determine optimal number of clusters (k=2 for income strata comparison).

methods.name: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
methods.description: Reduces dimensionality of the feature space to 2 components for visualization and improved clustering performance while retaining most variance in the data.

methods.name: Hierarchical clustering
methods.description: Uses agglomerative clustering to build a dendrogram and form clusters. Applies linkage criterion to determine cluster structure.

methods.name: Fuzzy C Means
methods.description: Applies fuzzy c-means clustering to allow partial membership of individuals in multiple clusters, providing soft clustering assignments.

metrics: Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) comparing cluster assignments to predefined income thresholds
Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) between cluster assignments and income categories
Silhouette Score for cluster cohesion and separation
Consistency ratio measuring how well each method's clusters align with income thresholds
evaluation.baseline: Predefined income thresholds ('>50K' vs '<=50K') serving as ground truth for cluster alignment
evaluation.success_criteria: K-means with PCA will show higher Adjusted Rand Index and Normalized Mutual Information scores compared to hierarchical clustering and fuzzy c-means when evaluated against predefined income thresholds, indicating better recovery of income strata consistency.

implementation_steps.description: Load uci_adult_census_income.csv using pandas, remove fnlwgt column, and encode categorical variables using pd.get_dummies()
Normalize numerical features using sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler and prepare feature matrix X and target vector y (binary income indicator)
Apply PCA transformation to reduce features to 2 components using sklearn.decomposition.PCA(n_components=2)
Implement K-means clustering with k=2 on both raw features and PCA-transformed features using sklearn.cluster.KMeans
Implement Hierarchical clustering using sklearn.cluster.AgglomerativeClustering with n_clusters=2
Implement Fuzzy C-Means clustering using scikit-fuzzy library or similar implementation
Calculate evaluation metrics (ARI, NMI, Silhouette Score) for each clustering method using sklearn.metrics
Compare cluster assignments against predefined income thresholds and compute consistency ratios
Generate summary statistics and visualizations comparing performance across all three methods

risks: Insufficient separation between income groups in the dataset to detect meaningful clustering patterns
Computational overhead from fuzzy c-means implementation potentially exceeding SLURM time limits
Potential overfitting or poor generalization due to small sample size relative to feature dimensions
